newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva gets FDA "approvable letter" for Copaxone.
newsitem.headline: Teva gets FDA "approvable letter" for Copaxone.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries said on Sunday it was informed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that it had accepted an advisory committee's recommendation concerning Teva's multiple sclerosis treatment Copaxone.
Teva said in a statement that the FDA accepted the recommendation that Copaxone "is an effective and safe treatment for patients with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis".

This is known as an "Approvable Letter" and is an important interim step on the way to final marketing approval. The letter was issued within two weeks of the advisory committee's recommendation that the FDA approve Copaxone.
"The company will now finalise all necessary steps, in full cooperation with the FDA, in order to obtain final marketing approval of the product in the near future," the statement said.

The panel's conclusion that the drug was safe and effective when used to reduce exacerbations of the disease cleared a major hurdle for the Israeli company as its expands its focus to research-based drugs. It has been known as a leading generic drug company.
The panel's recommendations are not binding but the regulatory agency typically follows the advice of its advisory committees.
Teva, Israel's biggest drug company, is traded both on Nasdaq and Tel Aviv.
